definition: A special balance sheet that the board prepares to test whether the company’s equity is below half of its registered share capital. It is prepared under the applicable annual accounts legislation, with the adjustments Section 14 permits, signed by the board and, where the company has an auditor, reviewed by that auditor.
The share capital stated in the articles of association and registered with the Swedish Companies Registration Office. It is the reference figure for the 50% and 100% tests in the procedure.
source: Ch. 1 Sec. 5 and Ch. 3 Sec. 1 Companies Act.

definition: In this procedure, the equity calculated under Section 14. That is ordinary equity, adjusted for assets recognised at a higher value or at net realisable value, for liabilities and provisions recognised at a lower value, and for certain State-aid liabilities. Untaxed reserves are split into an equity part and a deferred tax liability.

A general meeting that the board must convene as soon as possible when the control balance sheet shows equity below half of the registered share capital. It decides whether the company shall go into liquidation, and the control balance sheet and the auditor’s statement are presented there.

A new general meeting that must be held within eight months of the first, unless the first meeting resolved on liquidation or its control balance sheet showed equity of at least the registered share capital. A company reorganisation can push the deadline to two months after the reorganisation ends. A new, reviewed control balance sheet is presented.
The person who reviews the control balance sheet and gives a statement on it. The requirement applies only if the company has, or must have, an auditor.
source: Ch. 25 Secs. 13, 15–17 and Ch. 1 Sec. 12 b Companies Act.

definition: The winding-up of a company, in which liquidators realise the assets and pay the debts before the company ceases to exist. It is voluntary when the general meeting resolves on it, for example at a control meeting.

Liquidation ordered by the district court, for example when no second control meeting is held in time, or when the second meeting’s control balance sheet is not reviewed or does not show full share capital and the meeting has not resolved on liquidation.
A court-supervised procedure that gives a company in financial difficulty time to restructure its debts and continue trading.
source: the Company Reorganisation Act (lagen (2022:964) om företagsrekonstruktion).

definition: The Enforcement Authority’s collection of an unpaid debt by attaching the debtor’s property.
